Even a correct downstream response would show only some logical reachability, not connector seating, complete pinout/continuity, routing or signal margin, and the command may probe unrelated endpoints.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING CABLE IDENTITY AND COVERAGE DECISION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After ruling, use an endpoint-bound BMC/OOB transaction matrix for logical continuity and add owner-approved visual, pin-to-pin or oscilloscope evidence only if the specification requires physical assembly, continuity or signal-integrity coverage.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates different meanings of cable validation rather than treating a generic address scan as sufficient.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Logical endpoint reachability can miss swapped unused pins, intermittent contacts and marginal rise time; continuity can miss protocol behavior; neither alone proves all possible cable requirements.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Physical manipulation or measurement may require power isolation and human action, while active probing can disturb devices behind the cable; the final classification may change after scope is defined.

engineering_decision_request.question: Define Functionality row 1808 Wistron-HW-00010-V003 I2C Cable: exact harness PN/revision, endpoint boards/connectors/pinout/routing and whether required coverage is logical I2C reachability, physical assembly, continuity, signal integrity or separate checkpoints; then define BMC/OOB route, devices/responses, instruments/actions, acceptance, safe power state and recovery while preserving Master and requiring fresh review.

review_improvement: Distinguishes logical reachability from physical harness, pinout/continuity and signal-integrity validation, exposing why a generic bus scan cannot establish the named cable requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: A cable is an interconnect, not an addressable device. Seeing a downstream responder proves only that a subset of conductors and protocol timing worked at that moment; it may not prove every pin, connector retention or margin. Conversely, physical continuity does not prove correct protocol ownership. The missing specification must choose the intended evidence before automation can be classified safely.
